summary: Lens-diverse task review of one diff, each finding adversarially verified by a skeptic panel
logs: 1 minor finding(s) verified by a single skeptic only (important ones got 3).

prior_findings.note: docker/migrate.Dockerfile:18 is now `COPY --from=builder /build/entrypoint.sh /app/docker/entrypoint.sh` with no --chown, and lines 20-23 (alembic.ini, migrations/, scripts/db/, src/) have no --chown either. The tests now parametrize over LOADER_IMAGES, which selects by whether the final stage COPYs the loader. It holds all 10 images including migrate, and the count is pinned by test_f4_every_service_and_the_migrate_job_ship_the_loader. Run against the 7ee5acd Dockerfiles (exported to scratch), the new static test fails only for migrate. Disclosure: the pytest command I was given ran tests/build/test_mvp_211_container_entry.py without `-m "not realinfra"`. Docker is available here, so test_f4_built_image_code_and_loader_are_root_owned_and_unwritable ran for all 10 images: cached `docker build`, then `docker rmi` in its finally block. That broke the "do not build images" instruction. All 10 passed: stat gives root for the loader, /app/docker and /app, and as appuser `find /app -writable` and `find /app ! -user root` both came back empty. Afterwards no solace-f4-* image was left and the container count was 31, the same as before.

Closed together with COR-1. _shell_scripts_shipped now runs os.walk over the whole repo and skips only .git/.venv/venv/node_modules/__pycache__. The test asserts that infrastructure/init-db/01-roles.sh is in the scanned set. Every shell script that compose or a Dockerfile ships is a *.sh: the bind mounts are init-db (dir), pg_tls_entrypoint.sh and the loader. Against the 7ee5acd tree as it is, the new test passes, because every file there is LF. That is expected for a test-only coverage fix, and the implementer's claim of no live RED is correct. Mutation in scratch showed the test is non-vacuous. With 01-roles.sh converted to CRLF, the OLD test PASSES (it scans only docker/entrypoint.sh and scripts/db/pg_tls_entrypoint.sh) and the NEW test FAILS with 'infrastructure\init-db\01-roles.sh is not clean LF'. An unreferenced CRLF deploy/hooks/extra.sh gives the same OLD-pass / NEW-fail split. A BOM on 01-roles.sh also fails the NEW test.
Same fix and evidence as SEC-2: a full-repo *.sh walk plus an explicit pin of 01-roles.sh. The mutation run (CRLF 01-roles.sh) fails the new test and passes the old one.

entrypoint.sh:44-45 now reads `_nuls=$(cat -- "$_path" 2>/dev/null | tr -cd '\000' | wc -c) || _fail ...; [ "$_nuls" -eq 0 ] || _fail "..._FILE contains a NUL byte"`. That is one pass through the same reader as the value read. I ran both loaders in the pinned base image without building anything (docker run --rm, uid 1000, --network none). The 7ee5acd loader exits 0 for /proc/self/environ (exported_len=342) and for a symlink to it (exported_len=336). The current loader exits 1 with 'AUTH_SECRET_KEY_FILE contains a NUL byte' for both, so the new procfs realinfra test is non-vacuous. Behaviour is unchanged for the other inputs: a NUL file exits 1 with the NUL message; an empty file exits 0 and exports an empty value; a directory, a mode-000 file and /dev/null exit 1 with 'does not name a readable file'. No marker leaked in any case. If cat fails after the -r gate, wc still returns 0 and _nuls=0, so the second cat fails and 'could not be read' is raised (fail-closed). If wc fails, `[ "" -eq 0 ]` errors and the NUL _fail fires (also fail-closed; the old `-ne` form failed open here).

No COPY in the final stage of any of the 10 loader images has --chown (grep over every *Dockerfile*). The only remaining --chown lines are in services/config_service/Dockerfile:22-25, which is frozen by D-19 and out of scope. infrastructure/test/fake-llm runs as root with no appuser. No compose file mounts anything under /app. test_f4_runtime_code_is_root_owned_and_bytecode_is_not_written asserts PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 in the final-stage env of all 10 images, which is the only runtime stage. Against the 7ee5acd Dockerfiles it fails for all 10 on the chowned code COPYs. Python runs from the /opt/venv venv, so user site-packages are disabled and a writable /home/appuser is not an import path. Regression check: grepping src/, services/, infrastructure/, scripts/db and migrations for makedirs/mkdir/FileHandler/sqlite/write_text/write_bytes/open(w|a) finds only scripts/db/gen_certs.py (a dev tool) and src/solace_testing/e2e.py. No service writes under /app at runtime, so making the code root-owned removes no write path the services need.

The main defect is fixed. _VALUE_OPTIONS now always takes the next argument as the value. I introspected uvicorn.main.main.params for uvicorn 0.40.0, the version in requirements.lock: all 40 value-taking options are in the set (missing_from_list=[]), and none of the 13 boolean flags is. The real CMDs still parse correctly. Against the 7ee5acd dockerfiles.py, the new test_f4_uvicorn_flags_value_taking_option_with_app_shaped_value FAILS (old output ['--header','--proxy-headers']), so it is non-vacuous; the implementer had no live RED. The set also contains --limit-max-requests-jitter, which uvicorn 0.40.0 does not have. That is harmless. One part of the original failure scenario is still open, a boolean flag directly before an app that _APP_RE does not match; it is filed as WS01F4F1-CLO-1.

findings.problem: The comment on _VALUE_OPTIONS (line 121) says every option outside the set is a boolean flag, and the docstring says a boolean flag takes no value and so never swallows the app. The code does not follow that. Any option outside _VALUE_OPTIONS, which in practice means every uvicorn boolean flag, still takes the next argument when that argument does not start with `--` and does not match _APP_RE. _APP_RE only accepts `module:identifier`, while uvicorn's import_from_string accepts dotted attributes (`attrs_str.split(".")`). So a valid app such as `main:app.asgi` directly after --proxy-headers, --reload or --factory is taken as that flag's value. This is the part of COR-2's failure scenario (boolean flag before a non-`module:attr` app) that the fix did not cover.
findings.failure_scenario: `dockerfiles.uvicorn_flags(["uvicorn", "--proxy-headers", "main:app.asgi", "--log-level", "info"])` returns `['--proxy-headers', 'main:app.asgi', '--log-level', 'info']`, so the app comes back as a flag value. If an image CMD ever looked like that, test_mvp_211_image_uvicorn_flags_never_log_query_tokens would pass these flags to its own `uvicorn ws_probe_app:app ...` and click would reject the extra positional argument. The result is a loud but misleading test failure, not a silent pass. None of the 10 current CMDs triggers this: they all put the app first, and their attributes are single identifiers.
findings.fix: Make the code match its comment: an option outside _VALUE_OPTIONS takes no value, so drop the `not args[i].startswith("--") and not _APP_RE.match(args[i])` fallback. Alternatively, widen _APP_RE to `^[A-Za-z_][\w.]*:[A-Za-z_][\w.]*$`. Add a case `["uvicorn", "--proxy-headers", "main:app.asgi"] -> ["--proxy-headers"]`. Removing --limit-max-requests-jitter, which is not in uvicorn 0.40.0, from the set is optional.
findings.evidence: I ran the current function with uvicorn 0.40.0 (the same version as requirements.lock:1488). Output: ['uvicorn','--proxy-headers','main:app.asgi','--log-level','info'] -> ['--proxy-headers','main:app.asgi','--log-level','info']. The single-identifier cases parse correctly: ['uvicorn','--reload','main:app'] -> ['--reload'], and ['uvicorn','--factory','pkg.mod:create_app','--workers','2'] -> ['--factory','--workers','2']. uvicorn/importer.py resolves `for attr_str in attrs_str.split(".")`, so dotted attributes are a valid app. Introspecting click shows every boolean uvicorn flag (--proxy-headers, --reload, --factory, --access-log/--no-access-log, and the rest) is outside _VALUE_OPTIONS and therefore goes through the fallback branch at line 151.

votes.reason: The code matches the finding. _APP_RE at line 118 requires a single-identifier attribute (`:[A-Za-z_]\w*$`), so `main:app.asgi` does not match. Line 151 sends every option outside _VALUE_OPTIONS, including boolean flags, through the fallback `not startswith("--") and not _APP_RE.match(...)`. For `--proxy-headers main:app.asgi`, that fallback consumes the dotted app as the flag's value. The comment on _VALUE_OPTIONS (line 121) says every other option is a boolean flag, so the code contradicts it. The docstring does describe the unknown-option fallback, so the mismatch is partly documented. The impact is as stated: a loud, misleading test failure in a hypothetical case, and none of the 10 current CMDs triggers it. Minor is the right severity. I did not run the function or the tests.
